effects.log: You paint a small self-portrait, smiling, at the very edge. Then you lend it, and let it go.

events.text: At the market there is one grain seller, {npc}, whose scales are honest. Everyone knows it, and buys from {him}, and {his} neighbours, whose scales are not, hate {him} for it.

choices.text: Buy from {npc} and say why, loudly

mem.note: said it loudly at the market

effects.log: You say it loudly enough that two other stalls quietly adjust their scales that afternoon.

choices.text: Ask {him} why {he} bothers

effects.log: 'Because my father did not,' {npc} says, and sweeps the grain into your bag, and says no more about it.

events.text: The other grain sellers have accused {npc} of cheating, of all things, to the market inspector. {npc}'s honest scales are to be tested.

choices.text: Bring your own weighed bag as proof

effects.log: Your bag, weighed at home a hundred times, weighs exactly right on {npc}'s scales and light on everyone else's. The inspector is not pleased with the others.

choices.text: Gather the old customers to speak for {him}

effects.log: Thirty customers in a line, each with a story about {npc}'s honest measure. The inspector gives up and goes home.

events.text: {npc} is retiring. {His} scales, battered and honest, are going to the market itself, to hang at the gate as the measure anyone can check against.

choices.text: Be the first to check a bag against them

effects.log: Your bag weighs exactly right. You laugh, and so does {npc}, and the market applauds for no clear reason.

choices.text: Ask {him} what {he} will do now

effects.log: 'Buy grain,' {npc} says, 'and watch everyone's scales.' {He} becomes the terror of the market, and very happy.

events.text: The old ferry keeper has died, and the village needs someone to pole the ferry across the river until a new keeper is found. You know the river.

choices.text: Take the pole for a season

effects.log: You learn the current by its moods. You learn every person in three villages by the way they step into a boat.

choices.text: Help the village find a proper keeper

effects.log: A widow from upriver who grew up on boats. She takes the pole as if it were her own arm.

events.text: A season has become a year. The village has stopped looking for a new keeper. You have become the ferry.

choices.text: Accept it

effects.log: You build a little hut on the landing. You never charge the poor. The river becomes the most important thing you know.

choices.text: Train a young person to take over

effects.log: A restless youth from the village who needs a reason to stay. In a year the youth poles better than you.

events.text: In flood season you are poling the last crossing of the night when a voice calls from the far bank: someone who must cross, with a sick child.

choices.text: Cross in the flood

ok.log: Hard poling, the current tearing at the boat. You make the far bank and come back with the child and its parent, both soaked and alive. The healer is waiting at the landing.

fail.log: The current turns the ferry half round and you lose the pole. You paddle with your hands and make the bank far downstream, exhausted, the child safe.

choices.text: Shout to them to wait for first light, and keep a lantern lit all night

effects.log: You keep the lantern lit and talk to them across the river all night. At first light, the river calmer, you cross.

events.arc: The Lost Ring in the Well
events.text: A young neighbour has dropped a betrothal ring down the lane well and is in tears. The well is deep and cold and nobody wants to go down.

choices.text: Go down on the rope

ok.log: Cold water to the waist, the ring in the mud, and you come up with it in your teeth. The lane cheers. The betrothal goes ahead.

fail.log: You come up with a ring, but it is not the right ring: it is a much older one, with a name on it. Then you go down again and find the right one too.

choices.text: Fish for it with a magnet stone on a string

effects.log: Three hours of fishing. You bring up a ladle, two coins and, finally, the ring. The young neighbour hugs you.

events.arc: The Lost Ring in the Well
events.text: The young neighbour has married, and the couple want you at the place of honour, as the one who saved the ring.

choices.text: Sit there with dignity

effects.log: You sit very straight. Every guest is told the story, and you grow taller in each telling.

choices.text: Tell the story yourself, much bigger

effects.log: In your telling the well is a mile deep and full of eels. The children at the feast will never drink from it again.

events.arc: The Lost Ring in the Well
events.text: The couple's child is old enough to be told the story of the ring in the well, and comes to ask you if it is true.

choices.text: Show the child the well

effects.log: You lean over the edge together. The child's eyes go wide. 'You went down there?' 'I was younger. And so was the well.'

choices.text: Show the child the old ring you found

effects.log: The old ring with the name on it, from the bottom of the well. You have kept it all these years. You give it to the child, to keep.

events.text: The sword you carried as a young person hangs on the wall, its scabbard dusty. A neighbour's child, who has heard every story of the murim, stands under it every visit and stares.

choices.text: Take it down and let the child hold it

effects.log: The child holds it with both arms, solemn as a temple guardian, and nearly drops it. You catch it together. Neither of you breathes for a moment.

choices.text: Tell the child the true story of it

effects.log: The true story has much more walking and much less fighting than the child expected. The child listens to the end, disappointed and fascinated.

events.text: The child, taller now, asks you to teach the first three movements of the form you learned with that sword. Just three.

choices.text: Teach the three, with a stick

effects.log: Three movements, a thousand times, with a stick, in your yard. The child will remember them for the rest of a long life.

choices.text: Teach the first one only, and why

effects.log: One movement, and what it is for: stepping out of the way. The child thinks it is the dullest movement in the world. Years later the child writes to thank you.

events.text: The child is grown and setting off on the road, and has come to say goodbye. Your old sword is still on the wall.

choices.text: Give the sword

effects.log: You take it down and hand it over. Your wall looks strange for a month. Then it looks like a wall where a sword used to be, which is better.

choices.text: Keep the sword and give a walking staff instead

effects.log: 'The road is mostly walking,' you say. The young one laughs, and takes the staff, and comes back years later with it worn smooth.

events.text: You have never learned to ride. At your age, the horse trader says, people buy a donkey. You look at the donkey. The donkey looks at you with contempt.

choices.text: Buy the old grey mare instead (12 taels)

effects.log: The mare is older than the trader admits and gentler than any horse deserves to be. You fall off twice in the first week and she waits for you both times.

choices.text: Rent a horse for lessons (3 taels)

effects.log: A month of lessons in the trader's yard. You learn to fall properly, which the trader says is most of riding.

choices.text: Buy the donkey after all, for spite

effects.log: The donkey and you develop a deep and mutual respect based on stubbornness.

events.text: You and the grey mare have reached an understanding: she goes where she likes, slowly, and you pretend you chose it. Today she has taken you somewhere you have never been, a valley behind the hills.

choices.text: Let her keep going

effects.log: A waterfall, a ruined shrine, a meadow of wild irises. The mare grazes; you lie in the grass. You come home at dark and tell no one, because it is yours.

choices.text: Turn her back toward home

effects.log: She turns, sighing. On the way home she takes a different road anyway, past an orchard where someone gives you a basket of apricots.

events.text: The grey mare is very old now and cannot be ridden. She stands in your yard and greets you every morning with a rumble in her chest.

choices.text: Walk her to the iris valley once more, on foot

effects.log: Slowly, both of you. She grazes the irises. You sit by her until the sun goes. She dies in the spring, in the yard, in the sun.

choices.text: Keep her comfortable and talk to her each morning

effects.log: She listens to all your news. In the spring she lies down in the sun and does not get up. The lane helps you bury her under the apricot tree.

events.arc: The Child Lost at the Festival
events.text: In the crush of the Lantern Festival a very small child is standing alone by the bridge, too frightened even to cry, holding a rabbit lantern.

choices.text: Lift the child onto your shoulders

effects.log: From up there the child can see the whole crowd, and points, and shrieks: a parent, running the wrong way. You run after. The parent nearly faints with relief.

choices.text: Stay by the bridge and wait

effects.log: The parent will come back to where they lost the child. You buy the child a sugar figure and wait. An hour later a frantic parent comes back, as you knew they would.

events.arc: The Child Lost at the Festival
events.text: Every Lantern Festival since, the family of the lost child finds you in the crowd and brings you a rabbit lantern, by way of thanks.

choices.text: Hang the rabbit lanterns along your eaves

effects.log: A row of rabbits, one for every year. Children in the lane count them. So do you.

choices.text: Give each one to a child who has none

effects.log: Every year a child in the lane gets a rabbit lantern from the stranger who was once lost, and then found.

events.arc: The Child Lost at the Festival
events.text: The lost child is grown, and at this year's festival is standing by the same bridge with a small child on their shoulders, looking at the crowd for anyone lost.

choices.text: Stand beside them and help watch

effects.log: You watch the crowd together, the two of you, until the lanterns are put out. Nobody is lost this year.

choices.text: Buy a rabbit lantern for the small one

effects.log: The small one holds it exactly as a parent once did, by this bridge. Everything comes round.

events.text: You sleep badly now and walk the lane at the fourth watch. One night you meet {npc}, another old person who cannot sleep, sitting on the step of the closed teahouse.

choices.text: Sit down beside {him}

mem.note: sat on the step at the fourth watch

effects.log: You talk in whispers until dawn about nothing much. It is the best sleep you never had.

choices.text: Suggest a walk to the river

mem.note: walked to the river at night

effects.log: Two old people walking to the river in the dark, very slowly. The river is loud at night. You both feel younger and more tired.

events.text: There are five of you now at the teahouse step at the fourth watch, {npc} always the first. The night watchman has started bringing a pot of tea. You have, without meaning to, founded a society.

choices.text: Give it a name and rules

effects.log: The Society of the Sleepless. Rule one: no talk of illness. Rule two: see rule one. It lasts until someone mentions a knee.

choices.text: Keep it nameless and quiet

effects.log: No name, no rules, a pot of tea, the stars. It is the best club in the province because it does not know it is one.

events.text: {npc} has not come to the step for a week. You go to {his} house at the fourth watch, and find {him} asleep, deeply, for the first time in years, snoring like a tiger.

choices.text: Let {him} sleep

effects.log: You go back to the step and tell the others. The Society holds a celebration in whispers, with tea.

choices.text: Leave a cup of tea by the door for the morning

mem.note: left the tea at my door

effects.log: In the morning {npc} finds it, cold, and laughs, and comes to the step that night anyway, out of loyalty.

events.text: Your winter coat is thirty years old. It has been patched so often that the patches have patches. Your neighbours have started offering, delicately, to buy you a new one.

choices.text: Refuse: it is a good coat

effects.log: It is a good coat. It knows your shape. You wear it to the next festival with pride, and the patches tell your whole life to anyone who looks.

choices.text: Accept a new coat, and keep the old one in the chest

effects.log: The new coat is warm and stiff and does not know you. The old one lies in the chest smelling of thirty winters.

events.text: A neighbour's grandchild, sorting your chest for you, finds the old coat and asks what each patch is from.

choices.text: Tell the story of every patch

effects.log: The blue one from a fall on ice. The red one from a wedding. The square one from a fight with a goose. It takes all winter, one patch a night.

choices.text: Let the grandchild guess

effects.log: The guesses are wilder and better than the truth. You agree with all of them.

events.text: The grandchild has gone off into the world, and writes to ask for one thing from your house: the old coat, to wear on the road.

choices.text: Send it

effects.log: You send the coat with the next caravan. A year later a letter: the coat has a new patch, and a new story to go with it.

choices.text: Sew one last patch on it first

effects.log: Your hands are slow. The patch is crooked. You sew your own name inside it, small, and send it off.

events.text: You buy a chicken at the market for a festival dinner. On the way home it escapes, and runs into the lane, and the whole lane spends an hour failing to catch it.

choices.text: Dive for it

ok.log: You catch it in mid-air. The lane applauds. The chicken looks at you with such betrayal that you cannot bring yourself to cook it.

fail.log: You dive and land in a basket of radishes. The chicken watches from a roof. The lane is too busy laughing to help.

choices.text: Give up and buy tofu instead

effects.log: The chicken lives on the roofs of the lane like a bandit. You eat tofu, and it is a good dinner.

events.text: The escaped chicken has become the lane's chicken. It lays an egg on a different doorstep every morning. People consider it lucky to get one.

choices.text: Build it a coop at the lane's end

effects.log: It ignores the coop and sleeps on the shrine. The coop becomes the children's fort.

choices.text: Let it be free

effects.log: Free it stays. The day it lays an egg on your step you feel chosen, and tell everyone.

events.text: The lane's chicken has died of a great old age for a chicken. The lane holds a small and slightly ridiculous funeral.

choices.text: Give the eulogy

effects.log: You speak of its freedom, its eggs, its contempt for coops. People laugh and cry in equal parts.

choices.text: Plant a sunflower on its grave

effects.log: The sunflower grows taller than the wall and is full of seeds. The lane's new sparrows love it.
